title: Increase Image Size in KB — Photo Looks the Same, Free
description: Increase photo or signature size in KB to meet a form’s minimum, like 20 KB for IBPS photos. Pixels stay the same, it looks the same, nothing is uploaded.
intro: Your form says the photo must be at least 20 KB, but your file is only 12 KB? Increase the image size in KB here: pick the minimum, keep the same pixels, and download a file that passes the portal’s size check.

steps.name: Add your photo or signature
steps.text: Pick a JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC file from your phone or computer. It opens on your device and is never uploaded.

steps.name: Choose the minimum
steps.text: Tap 10, 20, 30, 50 or 100 KB, or type your own. Set the maximum from your form; each chip starts at a common range, such as 20–50 KB.

steps.name: Keep the pixels
steps.text: Leave Keep pixel size on so the width and height do not change. Turn it off only if a very large photo goes over the maximum.

steps.name: Check and download
steps.text: The pass check shows the new size against your range. When every row has a tick, download the JPG.

faq.q: Will increasing the KB make my photo blurry?
faq.a: No. Nothing is stretched or zoomed. The picture is saved at a higher quality, and any extra size comes from invisible noise or hidden data. Width and height stay the same.

faq.q: How do I increase photo size from 10 KB to 20 KB?
faq.a: Choose 20 KB as the minimum and set the maximum your form allows, for example 50 KB. The file lands a little above 20 KB, safely inside the range.

faq.q: Why do I get a JPG when I uploaded a PNG?
faq.a: Exam portals almost always ask for JPG or JPEG, and a JPG’s size can be tuned. A transparent PNG background becomes white.

faq.q: Can the portal see the added data?
faq.a: The added data is a standard JPEG comment block that every image viewer and portal skips. The portal reads the same picture; only the file size is bigger.

faq.q: Is my photo uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Everything runs in your browser. You can even switch on flight mode once the page has loaded.

sections.h2: Why exam portals set a minimum KB
paras: Most people look for ways to make a photo smaller, so a rule like “at least 20 KB” catches many applicants out. Notices rarely say why they set a minimum. The likely reason is quality: a very small file is often a thumbnail, a screenshot or a copy compressed many times, which prints badly on the admit card and is hard to match with your face at the exam centre.
Minimums in the official notices we track:
list: IBPS PO, IBPS Clerk, SBI and RBI: photo 20–50 KB, signature 10–20 KB, left thumb impression 20–50 KB, handwritten declaration 50–100 KB.
RRB NTPC, RRB ALP and RRB Group D: signature 30–49 KB.
NEET UG, JEE Main and CUET UG: photo 10–200 KB.
UPSC CSE: photo 20–200 KB, signature 20–100 KB.

sections.h2: How the size goes up without changing the photo
paras: A JPG’s size depends on its quality setting and on how much detail the picture has. First we save your picture again at a higher quality, which keeps it looking the same or a little cleaner. A plain picture, like a signature on white paper, can stay small even at the best quality. Then we add very faint noise of a level or two, which you cannot see, and if that is still not enough, a hidden comment block inside the file. That changes the file size, not the picture.
We count 1 KB as 1024 bytes and keep the file under your maximum even if the portal counts 1 KB as 1000 bytes.

Signatures are the most common case. A clean signature on white paper at 140×60 px is often only a few KB, while banking forms want at least 10 KB. If your form also fixes the pixels, use the Signature resize tool: it crops, cleans and fits the KB range in one go. If only the KB is wrong, choose 10 KB here and the maximum from your form.
